correctness.rationale: Prime-padding by isolated tripartite triangles preserves the sparse source promises and preserves triangle-partition feasibility in both directions. Applying the published marker-prime reduction after padding makes the common part size an odd prime p; every marker product is squarefree with at most three factors, so witness and cell periods are odd squarefree numbers with at most four and five prime factors. The LCM is exactly 3p times all marker primes, the GCD is exactly p, density remains one, and the unary output remains polynomially bounded. The finite arithmetic verifier agrees with these identities on representative parameters.

originality.rationale: The directly relevant 2026 primary sources were checked for odd-period, squarefree-period, bounded-prime-support, and equivalent exact-covering restrictions; no equivalent theorem was located. The current strong-hardness paper exposes the marker-product structure but does not state this prime-padding consequence. Classical odd/squarefree covering-system results concern structural existence, especially distinct moduli, and do not imply the computational hardness statement. The SCOPE archive has no pinwheel record. Priority risk remains elevated because the motivating preprint is new and the refinement is short once noticed.

value.rationale: The result shows that strong NP-completeness persists inside a rigid Chinese-remainder regime: every task period is a sparse divisor of one odd squarefree integer, all periods share exactly one common prime, and no period uses more than five prime factors. Thus evenness, repeated prime powers, and large prime support are not responsible for the hardness of the recent construction.
